body.p: Markdown documents are validated automatically as you type. The conversion engine continuously tries to parse your changes so that it can display the results in the Preview pane. If a change causes an error that prevents the parser from converting the syntax, an error message is displayed in the DITA tab or in the Results view at the bottom of the editor.
Examples of reported errors include headers that are in the wrong order or a document whose syntax begins with something other than a 1st level header.

section.title: Validating Markdown Against Schematron Using Built-in Scenarios
section.p:
Markdown documents can be validated with Schematron using the following built-in validation scenarios:
Validate Markdown Output as HTML (sample) - The Schematron is applied over the Markdown document's HTML output.
Validate Markdown Output as DITA (sample) - The Schematron is applied over the Markdown document's DITA output.
Validate Markdown Output - all checks (sample) - The Schematron is applied over the Markdown document's HTML and DITA output.

These scenarios are not active by default. Access them for Markdown documents by selecting the Configure Validation Scenario(s) from the Validation toolbar drop-down menutoolbar, or from the
Document Validate XML menu (or the Validate submenu when invoking the contextual menu on a file in the Project viewProject Explorer view).
The validation is done exclusively with Schematron, so the configuration dialog box accepts only .sch file. Add one validation unit per Schematron and output type (HTML or DITA).

You can also create your own validation scenarios for Markdown documents. In the scenario configuration dialog box, add a validation unit with the File type set to Markdown Document and select one of the following values in the Validation engine column:
Markdown as HTML Schematron Validator - The specified Schematron is applied over the HTML output of the Markdown document.
Markdown as DITA Schematron Validator - The specified Schematron is applied over the DITA output of the Markdown document.

Use the Specify Schema button to choose the Schematron file and, optionally, the Schematron phase to be applied. The schema type is always Schematron, since it is the only type of schema that can be used to validate Markdown documents.

section.title: Validating Markdown Against Schematron Using Global Associations
section.p:
You can configure a global association between Markdown documents and Schematron files by adding a catalog mapping for one of the following URIs:
http://www.oxygenxml.com/schematron/validation/markdown-as-html - The obtained Schematron will be applied over HTML conversions.
http://www.oxygenxml.com/schematron/validation/markdown-as-dita - The obtained Schematron will be applied over DITA conversions.

The catalog mapping is a fallback that is used only when the Markdown document does not have an associated validation scenario. If a validation scenario is associated, it takes precedence and the catalog mapping is ignored.If you are using a custom version of DITA-OT, the mapping information might not be generated properly, causing issues with Schematron validation. For example, error locations may not be accurate or synchronization may fail.

body.note: Markdown documents can be validated only with Schematron, either through a validation scenario or through a global association. If neither is configured, the document is not validated and no validation result is reported for it.

Inside the samples folder, there is a schematron-validation folder that contains files you can use to see how Schematron validation works with Markdown files. The path to the folder is: [OXYGEN_INSTALL_DIR]/samples/markdown/schematron-validation/.
